title: Layer conformance adjudication register
description: One JSON object per line in _bmad-output/ai-dlc-update/layer-adjudication-register.jsonl. A record is the operator's verdict on ONE row of a layer-contract clause at `level: ADJUDICATED`, keyed by the SUBJECT DIGEST that row fired on rather than by the entry's path. Keying by path would let one verdict clear every future change to the same entry, which is a permanent exemption wearing an adjudication's clothes; keying by the subject state means the duty re-fires the moment either side of the comparison moves. `reconcile/layer-drift.sh` is the single home of the digest computation and prints the digest in the blocking row, so the operator copies a value rather than deriving one. Once a verdict that carries `read` evidence (both members found) exists for a subject state its row stops blocking and `layer-drift.sh --list-adjudications <dist> <base> <theirs> <consumer>` is the read path for that digest, printing every keyed subject whether or not it still blocks. THE VERDICT VOCABULARY LIVES ONCE, in properties.verdict.enum below, ONE VALUE PER LINE: layer-drift.sh reads that array to decide whether a record satisfies the duty, and it does not restate it. The one-per-line layout is load-bearing for that reader — keep it.

clause.description: The layer-contract clause id this verdict answers, e.g. LC-E4.

entry.description: Consumer-relative path of the layer entry the row named, exactly as layer-drift.sh prints it in field 2.

subject_digest.description: Copied verbatim from the row `reconcile/layer-drift.sh` prints — the blocking row while it blocks, or, once any verdict exists for this subject state, `layer-drift.sh --list-adjudications <dist> <base> <theirs> <consumer>`, which prints every keyed subject whether or not it still blocks. Covers the entry file's content AND the hooked core file's content at the incoming ref, so it moves when either does.

verdict.description: A record whose verdict is outside this enum does not satisfy the duty. Otherwise any string would clear a blocking row and the adjudication would be a formality a typo passes.

recorded_utc.description: ISO-8601 UTC instant the verdict was recorded.

reason.description: Why. An adjudication with no stated reason is indistinguishable from a batch-clear, which is the failure mode this register exists to make visible.

supersedes.description: Required only when this record states a DIFFERENT verdict from an earlier record under the same key. Names what it overturns. Without it, two records under one key are a HARD-REGISTER-CONTRADICTION: the register would answer a lookup with whichever record happened to be read last, so LC-A1's blocking half would depend on file order.

owed.description: OPTIONAL. Work this verdict LEAVES OWED. A `still-additive` verdict that is only true because somebody plans to fix something has recorded a decision and lost the obligation: measured on the reference consumer, 5 of 46 rows encoded owed work in FREE PROSE, findable only by grepping reason fields for words like 'deferred' and 'still owed'. One of them read "Nothing but this reason field is tracking that debt." A debt nothing can enumerate cannot be acted on, and the register's three verdicts have no way to say 'keep it, and it is owed'.

id.description: Stable id a later record closes by name. Never reused.

what.description: The obligation, in the imperative. Not why the verdict was reached — that is `reason`.

closes_when.description: OPTIONAL. The observable condition under which this is dischargeable, so a reader can tell an owed item that is ready from one that is waiting.

closes_owed.description: OPTIONAL. Ids this record discharges. The register is append-only, so a debt is closed by a LATER row naming it, never by editing the row that opened it — the same supersession model `supersedes` already uses for verdicts.

withdraws.description: OPTIONAL. Retracts the REASON PROSE of earlier records on this SAME entry without changing any verdict. Each item is the `recorded_utc` of an earlier record on this record's `entry`, copied verbatim; every record on the entry at that instant is withdrawn (twin rows written at one instant under two clauses are one act and are withdrawn together). Use it when an earlier reason stated something that turned out false — an obligation that does not exist, most often — and the verdict itself stands, so `supersedes` (scoped to a DIFFERENT verdict) does not apply. The register is append-only, so a sentence is withdrawn by a LATER row naming it, never by editing the row that wrote it. `audit-layer-debt.sh` stops listing a withdrawn record under UNDECLARED, and reports under WITHDRAWALS THAT RESOLVE TO NOTHING any value that names no earlier record on the entry, names one at or after this record's own instant, or is not an array of strings. A withdrawn record's verdict still answers `layer-drift.sh` lookups; this field is read by the debt audit and nothing else.

read.description: Evidence that the entry was READ against the core change. Optional here so older records stay schema-valid, and REQUIRED FOR CLEARING: `layer-drift.sh` clears a row only for a record that carries it with both members found. Each member is ONE line copied verbatim from what was read, compared after tabs become spaces and leading and trailing whitespace is trimmed, at least 20 characters after trimming with at least 10 letters or digits, and not a markdown heading. The blocking row names where the core line must come from for its clause and never prints a line that would pass, so the evidence cannot be copied from the row. Without it, 0 of 1011 records on the reference consumer carried any sign of a read, and nine were written after a keyword grep and no Read call at all.

entry_line.description: A whole line of the BODY of the entry file the subject_digest pins, below its frontmatter.

core_line.description: A whole line of the clause's core-side text: an added or removed line of the range diff of the hooked file (LC-E4, LC-E6); a line of the declared extends: span at base or theirs (LC-E14); a line of the shadowed section at the entry's base_sha or at theirs (LC-O15); a line of the matched core section at theirs (LC-E19); a line of the target file at theirs (any other clause).
